//: Static deploy with one build step: pull Active Theory's assets into
assets/at/ so the deployed build matches a local run.
Why a build step rather than committing them: those files are Active
Theory's, and this keeps them out of the repository entirely while still
getting them into the deployed output. It is the same script used locally
(npm run fetch:assets), just run at build time. Without them the app falls
back to the procedural cloud and procedural textures, which renders
noticeably thinner -- the floret cloud is most of the look.
installCommand is skipped on purpose. The fetch script uses only Node
builtins, and the devDependencies (playwright, sharp, gltf-transform) are
heavy and only needed for local capture and asset compression.
--soft keeps a fetch failure from failing the whole deploy: the app has
working fallbacks for every one of these files, so a missing asset should
degrade the render, not break the site.
installCommand: echo 'skip install — fetch script needs only Node builtins'

headers.//: The GLBs and the point-cloud bake are content-addressed by name and never edited in place, so they can be cached hard.
Vendored three.js / Draco are pinned by the importmap and only change with a dependency bump.
